sentences.en: In 2011, the body of a woman was discovered in a California vineyard.
sentences.zh: 2011年，人们在加利福尼亚州的一处葡萄园内发现了一具女性尸体。

sentences.en: She had been decapitated, and her body had been drained of blood.
sentences.zh: 她被斩首，体内的血液也被放干。

sentences.en: It appeared her killer had gone to extraordinary lengths to conceal her identity.
sentences.zh: 凶手似乎费尽了心思来隐瞒她的身份。

sentences.en: For more than a decade, she was known only as Jane Doe.
sentences.zh: 十多年来，她一直被称为无名女尸。

sentences.en: Then, detectives finally learned her name, Ada.
sentences.zh: 随后，侦探们终于知道了她的名字——艾达。

sentences.en: But, identifying her only made this bizarre murder even more perplexing.
sentences.zh: 但是，确认她的身份反而让这起离奇的谋杀案更加扑朔迷离。

sentences.en: Ada is the new series from Casefile Presents, available now wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 《艾达》是“档案室呈现”推出的全新系列，各大播客平台现已上线。

sentences.en: Today's episode involves crimes against children, and won't be suitable for all listeners.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目涉及针对儿童的犯罪，并不适合所有听众收听。

sentences.en: It was 1.15pm on March 29, 1985, when Jean-Marie Villemin approached the La Roche's front door with a shotgun in hand.
sentences.zh: 1985年3月29日下午1点15分，让-马里·维尔曼手持猎枪走到了拉罗什家的前门。

sentences.en: Bernard had just arrived home with his wife, son, and father-in-law.
sentences.zh: 伯纳德刚刚和妻子、儿子以及岳父回到家中。

sentences.en: Jean-Marie raised his gun towards his cousin.
sentences.zh: 让-马里举枪指向他的表弟。

sentences.en: Taken aback, Bernard said,
sentences.zh: 伯纳德大吃一惊，说道：

sentences.en: Don't do anything stupid.
sentences.zh: 别做傻事。

sentences.en: He urged his cousin to put the gun down.
sentences.zh: 他劝表弟把枪放下。

sentences.en: I swear I didn't hurt your kid, Bernard said.
sentences.zh: 伯纳德说，我发誓我没有伤害你的孩子。

sentences.en: It wasn't me.
sentences.zh: 不是我干的。

sentences.en: He invited Jean-Marie to come inside so the two could talk.
sentences.zh: 他邀请让-马里进屋，好让两人谈谈。

sentences.en: Jean-Marie demanded answers.
sentences.zh: 让-马里要求给个说法。

sentences.en: He hadn't come with the intention to cause harm, but the more Bernard tried to placate him, the more overwhelmed Jean-Marie became.
sentences.zh: 他来的时候并非存心伤害，但伯纳德越是试图安抚他，让-马里就越感到情绪失控。

sentences.en: The words from the crow's letter haunted him.
sentences.zh: 那封神秘来信中的话语一直萦绕在他的脑海里。

sentences.en: I hope you die of grief.
sentences.zh: 我希望你痛不欲生。

sentences.en: He aimed the gun at Bernard's chest and pulled the trigger.
sentences.zh: 他将枪口对准伯纳德的胸口，扣动了扳机。

sentences.en: Jean-Marie Villemin had been astonished that the man he believed killed his son was allowed to walk free, while suspicion fell on his pregnant, grieving wife, Christine.
sentences.zh: 让-马里·维尔曼一直感到震惊的是，他认为杀害自己儿子的凶手可以逍遥法外，而怀疑的矛头却指向了他怀有身孕、悲痛欲绝的妻子克里斯蒂娜。

sentences.en: He had told the press that the investigators were doing everything they could to push her over the edge.
sentences.zh: 他曾向媒体透露，调查人员正竭尽全力把她逼上绝路。

sentences.en: He made no secret of the fact he wanted Bernard Laroche dead, even telling one journalist of his plans to pull off the assassination one month prior.
sentences.zh: 他毫不掩饰自己想要伯纳德·拉罗什死的心思，甚至在一个月前还向一名记者透露了自己实施谋杀的计划。

sentences.en: If the police weren't capable of getting justice for his son,
sentences.zh: 如果警方无法为他的儿子伸张正义，

sentences.en: Jean-Marie remarked,
sentences.zh: 让-马里表示，

sentences.en: I'll do the job myself.
sentences.zh: 那我就自己动手。

sentences.en: Before the shooting,
sentences.zh: 枪击事件发生前，

sentences.en: Jean-Marie was spotted loitering around Bernard's work and home on several occasions.
sentences.zh: 让-马里曾多次被目击在伯纳德的工作地点和住所附近徘徊。

sentences.en: Marie-Ange Laroche feared they'd be targeted and requested police protection.
sentences.zh: 玛丽-安热·拉罗什担心他们会成为袭击目标，于是请求警方提供保护。

sentences.en: Her requests were denied.
sentences.zh: 她的请求被拒绝了。

sentences.en: And now her husband lay in a pool of his own blood, the shotgun blasting a hole near his heart and killing him instantly.
sentences.zh: 而现在，她的丈夫倒在自己的血泊中，猎枪在他心脏附近轰出一个大洞，当场毙命。

sentences.en: Jean-Marie Villemin jumped in his car and raced to the hospital where his wife was still being cared for.
sentences.zh: 让-马里·维尔曼跳上汽车，直奔他妻子当时正在接受护理的医院。

sentences.en: He screamed as he told her what he'd done.
sentences.zh: 他尖叫着把自己的所作所为告诉了她。

sentences.en: He then turned himself in to police and was placed under arrest for the murder of Bernard Laroche.
sentences.zh: 随后，他向警方自首，并因谋杀伯纳德·拉罗什而被捕。

sentences.en: Press gathered outside the Laroche home and snapped photos as Bernard's body was wheeled away.
sentences.zh: 记者们聚集在拉罗什家门外，在伯纳德的尸体被推走时抓拍了照片。

sentences.en: Four days later, on Tuesday April 2, 1985, over 200 mourners gathered for Bernard's funeral.
sentences.zh: 四天后的1985年4月2日星期二，200多名哀悼者聚集在一起参加伯纳德的葬礼。

sentences.en: The family warned the press to keep at bay, but photographers still assembled at a safe distance.
sentences.zh: 家属警告媒体保持距离，但摄影师们仍然聚集在安全距离之外。

sentences.en: Bernard was laid to rest in Ormonse,
sentences.zh: 伯纳德被安葬在奥尔蒙斯，

sentences.en: This meant that even though the murder charges against Bernard Laroche were still active at the time he was shot,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，尽管在伯纳德·拉罗什被枪杀时，针对他的谋杀指控依然有效，

sentences.en: in his death he essentially benefited from the presumption of innocence.
sentences.zh: 但在他死后，他基本上享受到了无罪推定的待遇。

sentences.en: There would be no further investigation into his potential involvement in Gregory Villemin's murder.
sentences.zh: 有关他可能参与谋杀格雷戈里·维尔曼的调查将不再继续。

sentences.en: While Jean-Marie and Christine Villemin believed their son's death had now been avenged, many others disagreed.
sentences.zh: 虽然让-马里和克里斯蒂娜·维尔曼认为他们儿子的死现在已经报仇雪恨，但许多人并不这么认为。

sentences.en: In the eyes of the authorities, the public, and Bernard's anguished family members, a killer was still on the loose.
sentences.zh: 在当局、公众以及伯纳德痛苦的家属眼中，凶手依然逍遥法外。

sentences.en: And many believed they knew exactly who that killer was.
sentences.zh: 许多人坚信他们确切知道凶手是谁。

sentences.en: In late April, police conducted an extensive search of Jean-Marie and Christine's home.
sentences.zh: 四月下旬，警方对让-马里和克里斯蒂娜的住所进行了彻底搜查。

sentences.en: It was no longer occupied.
sentences.zh: 这里已经无人居住。

sentences.en: With her husband now in jail, Christine had gone to live with her grandmother in a small town roughly an hour's north of La Pange.
sentences.zh: 随着丈夫入狱，克里斯蒂娜搬去和外祖母同住，地点在拉庞日以北大约一小时车程的一个小镇上。

sentences.en: As police scoured the chalet, they were on the lookout for one item in particular.
sentences.zh: 当警方搜查这栋小木屋时，他们特别搜寻某一样物品。

sentences.en: In the cellar, they came across some sheets of metal that had been tied together with rope.
sentences.zh: 在地下室里，他们发现了用绳子捆在一起的几张金属板。

sentences.en: It was exactly what they were looking for.
sentences.zh: 这正是他们一直在寻找的东西。

sentences.en: Forensic analysis revealed that the rope in the Villemin's home was identical to that which was used to tie Gregory's hands and feet together.
sentences.zh: 法医分析显示，维尔曼家中的绳子与用来捆绑格雷戈里手脚的绳子一模一样。

sentences.en: Jean-Marie told police the rope came from his father, who had helped him with some work a few months prior to Gregory's death.
sentences.zh: 让-马里告诉警方，这根绳子是他父亲的，在格雷戈里死前几个月，他父亲曾帮他做过一些零活。

sentences.en: Jean-Marie said rope from the same bundle had also been used to fix the roof of Bernard LaRoche's car.
sentences.zh: 让-马里说，同一捆绳子也曾用来固定伯纳德·拉罗什汽车的车顶。

sentences.en: His father denied this.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲对此予以否认。

sentences.en: Although the discovery was compelling, it wasn't exactly the smoking gun investigators were hoping for.
sentences.zh: 尽管这一发现很有说服力，但它并不是调查人员一直期盼的决定性证据。

sentences.en: The rope was a common household item in the region, and most residents purchased their hardware from the same suppliers.
sentences.zh: 这种绳子是该地区的常见家居用品，大多数居民都是从同一家五金供应商那里购买的。

sentences.en: But when combined with the handwriting analysis and the reported witness sightings of Christine Villemin at the post office on the afternoon of Gregory's abduction,
sentences.zh: 但结合笔迹分析以及目击者报告称在格雷戈里被绑架那天下午看到克里斯蒂娜·维尔曼出现在邮局，

sentences.en: the circumstantial evidence against Christine was starting to mount.
sentences.zh: 对克里斯蒂娜不利的间接证据开始不断增加。

sentences.en: All that was missing was a motive.
sentences.zh: 万事俱备，只差一个动机。

sentences.en: With Bernard LaRoche out of the picture, tabloids ran wild with the possibility that Christine Villemin could be Gregory's real killer.
sentences.zh: 随着伯纳德·拉罗什出局，小报疯狂炒作克里斯蒂娜·维尔曼可能是格雷戈里真正的凶手的可能性。

sentences.en: A rumour gained traction that Bernard and Christine had been having an affair.
sentences.zh: 一则传言开始流传，称伯纳德和克里斯蒂娜曾有染。

sentences.en: Some wondered if Gregory found out about it and Christine killed him to ensure his silence.
sentences.zh: 有人怀疑格雷戈里是否发现了这件事，而克里斯蒂娜为了封口才杀了他。

sentences.en: Or, what if Bernard was really Gregory's biological father?
sentences.zh: 或者，伯纳德会不会真的是格雷戈里的亲生父亲？

sentences.en: Maybe Christine had killed Gregory because she could no longer stand the living, breathing proof of her adultery.
sentences.zh: 也许克里斯蒂娜杀死格雷戈里是因为她再也无法忍受这个她不忠行为的活生生的证据。

sentences.en: Christine told reporters it wasn't her job to convince the public she was innocent.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜告诉记者，说服公众自己是无辜的并不是她的工作。

sentences.en: All that mattered was what the authorities believed.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是当局怎么想。

sentences.en: The public scrutiny became so intense that she avoided going out altogether.
sentences.zh: 公众的密切关注变得如此严密，以至于她干脆避免出门。

sentences.en: Authorities still hadn't managed to uncover any evidence that Christine had been unfaithful to Jean-Marie.
sentences.zh: 当局仍然未能查明任何能证明克里斯蒂娜对让-马里不忠的证据。

sentences.en: But there were whispers that their marriage wasn't the solid, united front they presented to the media.
sentences.zh: 但有传言称，他们的婚姻并不像他们在媒体面前表现得那么坚不可摧、团结一致。

sentences.en: Christine had met Jean-Marie when she was just 16.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜认识让-马里时年仅16岁。

sentences.en: He was her first and only love, and they'd been inseparable ever since.
sentences.zh: 他是她的初恋，也是唯一的爱，从那以后他们就形影不离。

sentences.en: There were whispers about domestic violence.
sentences.zh: 当时流传着关于家庭暴力的传闻。

sentences.en: Christine claimed Jean-Marie had slapped her once in 1979.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜声称让-马里曾在1979年扇过她一巴掌。

sentences.en: She'd gone to stay with her mother and they'd reconciled quickly after that.
sentences.zh: 她曾去和母亲同住，在那之后他们很快就和好了。

sentences.en: Investigators wondered whether Christine could have killed Gregory to spite her husband for mistreating her in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 调查人员怀疑克里斯蒂娜是否会为了报复丈夫过去虐待自己而杀害格雷戈里。

sentences.en: The possibility was also floated that Christine could be mentally ill and had killed Gregory during some kind of psychotic episode.
sentences.zh: 还有人提出这样一种可能性：克里斯蒂娜可能患有精神疾病，在某种精神病发作期间杀害了格雷戈里。

sentences.en: Maybe she didn't want to spite Jean-Marie at all, but was jealous of his love for Gregory and wanted her husband's attention all for herself.
sentences.zh: 也许她根本不是想报复让-马里，而是嫉妒他对格雷戈里的爱，想要独占丈夫的关注。

sentences.en: A month after Bernard LaRoche's murder,
sentences.zh: 在伯纳德·拉罗什被谋杀一个月后，

sentences.en: Jean-Marie Villemin participated in an official reenactment of the shooting.
sentences.zh: 让-马里·维尔曼参与了谋杀枪击案的官方情景重演。

sentences.en: Although it was standard police practice, it was a media spectacle, with hordes of press in attendance.
sentences.zh: 尽管这是标准警方程序，但这却是一场媒体奇观，大批记者到场。

sentences.en: Fears of further vigilante justice were so strong that Jean-Marie was required to wear a bulletproof veSt.
sentences.zh: 人们对进一步发生私刑正义的恐惧如此强烈，以至于要求让-马里必须穿上防弹背心。

sentences.en: He remained in custody, awaiting trial.
sentences.zh: 他继续被拘留，等待审判。

sentences.en: Christine visited him several times a week, never budging from her stance that the husband and wife were anything other than completely united.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜每周去看望他好几次，始终坚持夫妻二人完全一条心的立场没有一丝动摇。

sentences.en: By the start of July 1985,
sentences.zh: 到1985年7月初，

sentences.en: Christine was six months pregnant.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜已经怀孕六个月。

sentences.en: For eight and a half months, her son's unsolved murder and the subsequent events had dominated national news.
sentences.zh: 在八个半月的时间里，她儿子未破的谋杀案以及随后的事件一直占据着全国新闻的主导地位。

sentences.en: As journalist Michael Dobbs wrote in the Washington Post,
sentences.zh: 正如记者迈克尔·多布斯在《华盛顿邮报》上写道：

sentences.en: Who killed Petit Gregory?
sentences.zh: 谁杀了小格雷戈里？

sentences.en: Wherever you go in France this summer, there is no escaping the insistent question.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，无论你走到法国的哪个角落，都无法避开这个执着的问题。

sentences.en: It screams at you from the front pages of newspapers and the covers of news magazines.
sentences.zh: 它从各大报纸的头版和新闻杂志的封面朝你大喊大叫。

sentences.en: It turns up in endless conversations on trains, in working-class bistros, on the beach, at dinner parties.
sentences.zh: 它出现在火车上、工人阶级的酒馆里、海滩上、晚宴上的无休止交谈中。

sentences.en: But the press were running out of new angles to cover.
sentences.zh: 但媒体已经快找不到新的报道角度了。

sentences.en: Relatives of those involved and village locals had long grown weary of the incessant media attention, with some displaying signs on their doors that read,
sentences.zh: 涉案人员的亲属和村里当地人早已对没完没了的媒体关注感到厌烦，一些人在门上贴出了标语写道：

sentences.en: The public wanted justice and investigators were eager to close the case once and for all.
sentences.zh: 公众渴望正义，调查人员也急于彻底结案。

sentences.en: On Friday July 5,
sentences.zh: 7月5日星期五，

sentences.en: Christine Villemann was arrested and charged with Gregory's murder.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·维尔曼被捕并被控谋杀格雷戈里。

sentences.en: Christine was unwavering in her claims of innocence.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜坚称自己无罪，态度坚定不移。

sentences.en: After six days in custody, she announced she was going on a hunger strike unless she was released from remand.
sentences.zh: 在被拘留六天后，她宣布如果不被释放候审，她将绝食抗议。

sentences.en: News of the strike reached her husband in prison and he too stopped eating.
sentences.zh: 绝食的消息传到狱中的丈夫耳中，他也停止了进食。

sentences.en: Five days into the strike, the courts agreed that there wasn't enough evidence to warrant holding Christine behind bars.
sentences.zh: 绝食五天后，法院同意没有足够证据证明将克里斯蒂娜收押在监是合法的。

sentences.en: She was released under judicial supervision to await trial in her grandmother's care.
sentences.zh: 她在司法监督下获释，在祖母的照顾下等待审判。

sentences.en: By this point, several media outlets had labelled Christine Villemann the most hated woman in France.
sentences.zh: 此时，几家媒体已经将克里斯蒂娜·维尔曼贴上了法国最令人讨厌的女人的标签。

sentences.en: Adding fuel to the fire was a controversial article published in the popular daily newspaper,
sentences.zh: 火上浇油的是，《解放报》这家受欢迎的日报上发表了一篇引发争议的文章。

sentences.en: Liberation.
sentences.zh: 《解放报》。

sentences.en: Titled,
sentences.zh: 题为，

sentences.en: Sublime,
sentences.zh: 崇高，

sentences.en: Necessarily Sublime,
sentences.zh: 必然崇高，

sentences.en: Christine V.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·V。

sentences.en: The article was written by Marguerite Duras, a famous writer known as one of France's most important literary figures.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章由玛格丽特·杜拉斯撰写，她是一位著名的作家，被视为法国最重要的文学人物之一。

sentences.en: Duras was convinced of Christine's guilt.
sentences.zh: 杜拉斯坚信克里斯蒂娜有罪。

sentences.en: She reported that Jean-Marie had once hit Christine because she overcooked some steaks.
sentences.zh: 她报道说，让-马里曾因克里斯蒂娜把牛排烤过头而打过她。

sentences.en: Duras wrote that Christine lay awake at night fantasising about gouging out her husband's eyes.
sentences.zh: 杜拉斯写道，克里斯蒂娜夜不能寐，幻想着挖出她丈夫的眼睛。

sentences.en: In Duras' opinion,
sentences.zh: 在杜拉斯看来，

sentences.en: Christine felt trapped in her marriage and never wanted to be a mother.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜感到自己被困在婚姻中，并且从来不想当母亲。

sentences.en: Killing Gregory and encouraging Jean-Marie to avenge his death by shooting Bernard Laroche was a way to free her of both traps.
sentences.zh: 杀死格雷戈里并鼓励让-马里枪杀伯纳德·拉罗什以报杀子之仇，是让她摆脱这双重困境的一种方式。

sentences.en: It was the perfect plan.
sentences.zh: 这是一个完美的计划。

sentences.en: Duras wrote,
sentences.zh: 杜拉斯写道：

sentences.en: No man in the world can know what it's like for a woman to be taken by a man she doesn't desire.
sentences.zh: 世上没有任何男人能体会一个女人被她并不渴望的男人占有所经历的感受。

sentences.en: Marguerite Duras had never met Christine.
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特·杜拉斯从未见过克里斯蒂娜。

sentences.en: She based her opinion mostly on a feeling that she had upon seeing the Villemann's home in La Panche.
sentences.zh: 她的看法主要基于她在看到维尔曼位于拉庞日的住所时产生的某种感觉。

sentences.en: Although the article was prefaced with a warning that the work was purely the view of the writer, it had a huge influence on public opinion.
sentences.zh: 尽管这篇文章在开头加了警告，称该作品纯属作者个人观点，但它对公众舆论产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Wanting to avoid another
sentences.zh: 为了避免重蹈
